title: Add vow-lean-kernel checker
body:
Adds a checker for **[vow-lean-kernel](https://github.com/pmatos/vow-lean-kernel)** — a Lean 4 kernel written in [**Vow**](https://github.com/vow-lang/vow), a young systems language. It's a fresh, independent implementation in a host language not yet represented in the arena, so it adds to the implementation diversity the arena is after.

### What it is

A `url`-type checker. `build` self-hosts the Vow compiler (`vowc`) from `vow-lang/vow` at a pinned commit, then builds the kernel with it (the kernel builds only with the self-hosted `vowc`); this mirrors the project's own CI. `run` reads the NDJSON and exits per the arena protocol.

Needs `cargo`/Rust and `git` at build time (both already used by other checkers here, e.g. nanoda).

### Coverage

- Accepts the full **tutorial** suite and all of Lean core **`Init`** (54,475 declarations).
- Nat arithmetic uses a base-2³² bignum backend, so reductions past 2⁶⁴ are exact.
- Declarations beyond the currently supported fragment are **declined** (exit 2), never falsely rejected — sound on what it accepts, conservative elsewhere.

### Dry-run (local, `ulimit -v 12G`)

| test | verdict | notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| init | **accept** | all 54,475 core `Init` declarations |
| std | **decline** | exhausts the memory budget partway |
| mathlib | **decline** | the full export exceeds the budget while loading |

No false rejects and no crashes. One implementation note baked into `run`: the Vow runtime exits `1` on OutOfMemory, which would collide with the arena's *reject* code, so an OOM is detected and reported as a **decline** instead (tracked upstream as [vow-lang/vow#877](https://github.com/vow-lang/vow/issues/877)).

### Validation

- `checker.yaml` validates against `schemas/checker.json`.
- The `build` was reproduced from a clean checkout (fresh `vow-lang/vow` clone → `cargo build --all` → self-hosted `vowc` → `lean_checker`).
- The project's tutorial suite passes 131/131 on the resulting binary.

title: Add proj-of-prop soundness test
body:
The exported theorem builds a proof of `False` via a projection from a
`Prop`-typed structure whose constructor was applied to an ill-typed
argument:

    structure Wrapper : Prop where mk :: p : False
    theorem badFalse : False := (Wrapper.mk True.intro).p

A checker that types a projection by inferring (rather than checking)
its structure — trusting the structure to be well-typed rather than
verifying the constructor's arguments against its binders — will accept
this and return `badFalse : False`. A sound checker must reject it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: Add the Sonanoda kernel to the arena
body:
This PR adds the Sonanoda kernel to the arena.

Sonanoda is an experimental, minimally modified variant of Nanoda with a more efficient definitional equality check. When comparing proof terms, it skips comparing their types when it seemed safe.

On my local machine, Sonanoda is 31% faster than Nanoda in the arena. In pathological situations such as simplifying `xs[xs[xs[...[xs[0 + i]]]]]`, I found that Sonanoda's optimization can mean the difference between quadratic and linear time.

title: bump nanobruijn: lean Expr, cache cleanup
body:
Update nanobruijn to 99e58d6. Key changes since 97a206e:

- Remove num_loose_bvars and has_fvars fields from Expr variants.
  nlbv lives only in the parallel expr_nlbv Vec; has_fvars becomes lazy
  memoized (only queried on non-hot paths). mk_app is now pure ExprPtr
  arithmetic. Init -6.6%.
- Compute Expr hash on demand (removed the stored hash field).
- Remove caches subsumed by UF or by alloc_expr hash-consing:
  defeq_pos, mk_pi_cache, mk_lambda_cache, strong_cache, eq_cache.
- Add is_* head-check helpers and view_*_head partial views; hot paths
  avoid the expensive view_expr body-traversal where a tag check or
  subset of children suffices.
- unfold_pi_step / unfold_lambda_step helpers marked #[inline] for
  binder-telescope walks.

title: Add shift-cascade test
body:
## Summary
- New test: N=1000 nested `let` bindings inside a lambda, each referencing the outer parameter
- Targets O(N²) substitution overhead in de Bruijn kernels with deferred shifts
- O(N) in locally-nameless kernels
- Moves perf micro-benchmarks (app-lam, grind-ring-5, shift-cascade) into `tests/perf/`
- Supports recursive YAML loading so test names can include subdirectory paths (e.g., `perf/shift-cascade`)

## Structure
```lean
fun (a : Nat → Nat) =>
  let f₁ := fun x => a x
  let f₂ := fun x => a (f₁ x)
  ...
  let fₙ := fun x => a (fₙ₋₁ x)
  fₙ 0
```

Each `let` substitution creates shifted copies of values with free bvars. In a shift-based kernel, `Shift(val, offset)` wrappers accumulate and each subsequent substitution must traverse through all previous wrappers.

## Measurements (N=1000)

| Checker | Time |
|---------|------|
| Official Lean kernel | 51ms |
| nanoda (locally-nameless, Rust) | 1ms |

Scaling confirmed O(N²): N=500 → 26ms, N=1000 → 139ms in a shift-based checker.

title: test: add lean4lean level normalization exploit
body:
**Disclaimer:** exploit found by Opus 4.6, PR opened by Opus 4.6; see [Zulip thread](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219941-Machine-Learning-for-Theorem-Proving/topic/Proofs.20of.20false.20found.20by.20Opus.204.2E6/with/576462943).

This PR adds a proof of False that exploits a bug in lean4lean's level normalization algorithm (`Level.lean`).

**Bug:** The `normalizeAux` function in the `.imax u (.param v)` case drops the accumulated offset `k` when `k > 0`. Specifically, `addNode v path'` adds `v+0` instead of `v+k`, and the `v=0` case is missing `addConst k path`. Combined with the `addConst` optimization that skips `k=1` on non-empty paths, this causes `isEquiv'(imax 0 v, succ(imax 0 v)) = true` even though these levels differ at `v=0` (0 vs 1).

**Exploit chain:**
1. `down.{v} : Sort(succ(imax 0 v)) → Sort(imax 0 v)` := id (accepted by the level bug)
2. `myProp : Prop := down.{0} Bool` (declared type `Prop` avoids structural `isProp` check issue; `isDefEq(Sort(imax 0 0), Sort 0)` passes via `isEquiv'(imax 0 0, 0) = true`)
3. Proof irrelevance on `myProp` (a `Prop`) equates `Bool.true` and `Bool.false`, then `Bool.rec` maps `true → True` and `false → False` to derive `False`.

Tested against digama0/lean4lean (commit `e5751bf`, Lean toolchain v4.26.0): lean4lean accepts all declarations including `proof_of_false : False`.

title: Add two nanoda soundness exploit tests
body:
**Disclaimer:** tests found by Opus 4.6, PR opened by Opus 4.6; see [Zulip thread](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219941-Machine-Learning-for-Theorem-Proving/topic/Proofs.20of.20false.20found.20by.20Opus.204.2E6/with/576462943).

Two proof-of-False NDJSON export files that exploit bugs in nanoda (version `93bf604bacf5fd5aa45d153b4264c2b8265db01f`). Both should be rejected by correct checkers.

**Bug 1 — `nanoda-leq-core`:** The `IMax` reflexivity case in `leq_core` (level.rs:188) returns `true` for `leq(imax(u,v)+1, imax(u,v))` because it checks structural equality without verifying `diff >= 0`. This allows defining a universe-collapsing identity `down.{u,v} : Sort(succ(imax(u,v))) → Sort(imax(u,v))`, which casts between `True` and `False` via `Bool.rec` at `Sort(imax(0,0)) = Prop`.

**Bug 2 — `nanoda-nat-rec-rules`:** `assert_nonnested_recursors_def_eq` (inductive.rs:1230) compares imported `rec_rules` against themselves (`rec_rules.iter().zip(rec_rules.iter())`) instead of against the independently constructed rules. This lets us define `Nat` with a wrong succ rule (always returns `hzero`). Combined with nanoda's nat literal extension — which hardcodes correct arithmetic for concrete `NatLit` args but falls back to the wrong `Nat.rec` for symbolic args — this creates an inconsistency that yields `False`.

title: fix: add pkg-config to Nix devShell for libffi discovery on bare machines
body:
On minimal self-hosted runners (bare Hetzner), the RPython/PyPy translation step for `rpylean` fails because `pkg-config` is absent from the system PATH — GitHub-hosted runners have it pre-installed, bare machines do not.

The PyPy RPython translator calls `pkg-config libffi --libs-only-L` at compile time to locate `libffi`. Without the binary:

```
ValueError: running 'pkg-config libffi --libs-only-L' failed:
[Errno 2] No such file or directory
and the default ['/usr/lib/libffi'] is not a valid directory
```

## Changes

- **`flake.nix`**: Add `pkg-config` to `buildInputs`. The already-present `libffi.dev` provides the `libffi.pc` file; Nix's `mkDerivation` devShell automatically populates `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` from `buildInputs`, so `pkg-config` can resolve `libffi` entirely from the Nix store.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Create a pull request to fix a CI/runtime discrepancy between GitHub-hosted runners and a self-hosted bare Hetzner machine for repository `leanprover/lean-kernel-arena`.
> 
> Context:
> - The workflow/job in question: https://github.com/leanprover/lean-kernel-arena/actions/runs/22253568227/job/64381121998
> - On GitHub-hosted runners, the job works.
> - On the self-hosted bare machine, it fails because `libffi` is not being found/loaded by Python at runtime.
> - The repository uses Nix (a nix shell/devShell) and `libffi` is included in the Nix environment, but the Python code is still picking up the system environment (where `libffi` isn’t installed) rather than the Nix-provided `libffi`.
> 
> Goal:
> Ensure that when running under the provided Nix shell/devShell (including in CI), the Python code reliably picks up the Nix-provided `libffi` (e.g., via correct environment variables, rpath, or Python package configuration), so behavior matches GitHub-hosted runners and self-hosted machines.
> 
> Requirements:
> 1. Investigate where Python is trying to load `libffi` (likely via `ctypes` / `cffi` / `ffi` bindings) and why it succeeds on GitHub-hosted runners but fails on self-hosted.
> 2. Update Nix configuration and/or runtime environment to ensure the dynamic loader can find `libffi` from the Nix store when running the Python entrypoints/tests.
>    - Possible solutions include setting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` (if relevant), `NIX_LDFLAGS`, `LIBRARY_PATH`, `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, `CFLAGS/LDFLAGS`, `CTYPESGEN`, patching wrappers, or using `makeWrapper`/`wrapProgram` to inject needed env vars.
>    - Prefer an approach that is robust and minimal, and doesn’t rely on system-wide packages.
> 3. Add/adjust CI or a small regression test that exercises the Python code path that loads `libffi`, ensuring failure would be caught on machines without system `libffi`.
> 4. Keep the solution Nix-centric: the nix shell should provide everything needed.
> 
> Deliverables:
> - A PR with changes to the relevant Nix files (e.g., `flake.nix`, `shell.nix`, `default.nix`, etc.) and/or Python startup code/wrappers so `libffi` is found.
> - Clear commit message(s) and a short PR description explaining the root cause and fix.
> 
> Notes:
> - Assume the self-hosted machine is a minimal Linux environment where only Nix-provided dependencies are available.
> - Ensure the solution works both for `nix develop` (or equivalent) and for CI workflows.
> 


</details>

title: Tutorial declarations for all export-format cases
body:
I'm in the midst of porting a parser from the old line format to NDJSON, and the tutorial is pretty useful for doing so, but it doesn't fully cover the [export format](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4export/blob/master/format_ndjson.md). Here's a list of what's currently not emitted by any declaration in it:

```
    LitStr,
    LitNat,
    Proj,
    Let,
    RecRule,
    Recursor,
    UniverseMax,
    Constructor,
    InductiveSkeleton,
    Opaque,
    Axiom,
    Quot,
```

(Also not present are binder types other than `default`.)

Is a PR adding declarations which force emitting each of these as well welcome for the tutorial file, or would you prefer a separate file which has an explicit goal to exercise all of the export format rather than be illustrative of the type checker features?

Relatedly is [these tests](https://github.com/leanprover/lean-kernel-arena/blob/a7a20efb7d40b8aba9344e2936d4b7f16c42b3bf/tutorial/Tutorial.lean#L31-L38) might be written that way intending that they emit `max` / `imax` lines, but they don't, they just end up being:

```json
{"i":0,"sort":{"u":1}}
{"i":1,"sort":{"u":0}}
```
